Meeting header:
- Date: 2029-06-18

- Duration: ~52 minutes
- Attendees: Jordan Park (Redwood AE), Samira Khan (Redwood SE), Liam O'Connor (Redwood SE), Dr. Priya Menon (Elmwood CTO), Carlos Reyes (Head of Security), Aisha Turner (Platform Eng), Evan Li (Data governance)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be imperfect):
Redwood and Elmwood discussed POC scope for a security-focused pilot: success criteria (latency/cost/accuracy thresholds), workload sizing for benchmarks, timelines for a 4-week pilot, and security/compliance requirements including SOC 2/ISO attestation, SSO/SAML integration, RBAC, audit logs retention, KMS integration and VPC/connectivity options. Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Park: hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'll kick off, hey priy aisha carlos, thanks for taking the time, today we want to run through the poc scope for the security pilot and make sure we have clear success criteria and timeline, i'll hand over to samira in a sec to talk benchmarks
[00:18] Dr. Priya Menon: thanks jordan, yeah our board asked for a tight pilot we have to validate the security controls and the perf implications before we go to procurement, we also need to confirm data residency and ph I constraints, so those are big for us
[00:34] Carlos Reyes: hi all, from security i want to ensure we get SOC 2 and ISO attestation, SSO via our IdP and RBAC controls, also audit logs with immutable retention, and KMS integration or HSM if possible, we have to prove chain of custody for prompts and model outputs
[00:52] Samira Khan: got it, and from the infra/bench side we typically run 3 workload profiles: small interactive chat, mid-sized batch emb generation, and high-throughput bursty inference to test scaling and latency tail; for the pilot we can size VMs/gpus to match your expected peak qps, can you share typical qps and seq lengths?
[01:12] Aisha Turner: sure, baseline: interactive clinical triage chat, avg payload ~350 tokens, peak concurrent users ~120, average qps around 15 sustained with bursts to 80 for short windows; embeddings jobs are batched nightly, ~50k records, that's not live but we want to test throughput and cost per embedding
[01:30] Liam O'Connor: quick follow, when you say 350 tokens that's around 1.2k context-ish for some of our models but ok, we'll map to sequence lengths; for benching we usually run realistic prompt sets and a de-id dataset; also we'll instrument KV cache behavior and warm starts to emulate production
[01:46] Evan Li: our retention policy for pilot logs: 6 months for full audit logs, but any PHI must be excluded from test data — pilot must run on de-identified data or synthetic data. we also require the ability to export logs for our SIEM
[02:02] Jordan Park: great, so to confirm initial success criteria — for the security pilot we propose: SOC2 + ISO attestation provided, SSO integrated, RBAC enforced for at least 3 roles, audit logs with X fields and 6-month export, and perf targets: p95 latency under 800ms for interactive profile and embedding throughput of Y per hour. does that align?
[02:24] Carlos Reyes: that sounds close. on RBAC we need fine-grained control — mapping to AD groups, ability to restrict model access and to require approval for export of outputs. Also need proof of encryption at rest using our KMS, ideally a customer-managed key option
[02:42] Samira Khan: we support customer-managed KMS for Private and Dedicated deployments; for Hosted we have bring-your-own-key for encryption at rest via integrated KMS; small correction, sometimes our naming confuses folks — "Redwood Dedicated" shows up as "Redwood Dedicate" in some docs, sorry, 
[02:58] Dr. Priya Menon: another question, timeline wise we have a compliance window — can we do a 4-week pilot? week 0 prep, week 1 integration (SSO, networking), week 2 benchmarks, week 3 validation and security review, week 4 exec summary and procurement handoff
[03:18] Jordan Park: that's the exact cadence we've done before. for week 1 we'll need SSO metadata and a test account, staging VPC peering or secure tunnel, and the de-identified test workload. samira, i'll let you run through the bench plan
[03:34] Samira Khan: bench plan: day 1 smoke tests w/ a small set of prompts, day 2 full interactive suite to capture latency and p95/p99, day 3 embeddings throughput run with batching and quant settings, day 4 stress test with burst traffic to observe autoscale and fallback behavior; we'll record token costs and latency breakdowns per route. note: some transcribed names may show up weirdly in logs, e.g., K V cache as "K V cash" in auto-transcripts, just FYI
[03:58] Aisha Turner: on networking, we prefer VPC peering to avoid public egress; is that available for the hosted pilot?
[04:08] Liam O'Connor: yes, we offer secure peering for Hosted for enterprise pilots; we can also run in Dedicated pool or Private appliance if you require complete isolation. each option has different lead times — Hosted with peering is fastest (~2-3 days once metadata is in), Dedicated takes provisioning (~2-3 weeks), Private on-prem longer
[04:28] Carlos Reyes: provisioning lead times matter. procurement needs a clear timeline and an SLA. also, can you provide sample audit log schema? we need to verify fields like user_id, role, timestamp, request_payload_hash, model_id, model_version, response_hash, action_type, region, and KMS_key_id
[04:46] Samira Khan: yes we have a standard audit schema, we'll share the JSON; it will include those fields plus request/response size, latency ms, tokens_in/out. logs are immutable with HMAC so you can ingest to your SIEM. we can also stream logs to an S3 endpoint in your account
[05:04] Evan Li: good. for SSO we use Okta, SAML metadata should be straightforward. we also require session timeouts and MFA for admin roles
[05:14] Jordan Park: MFA for admin roles and session ttl can be enforced via RBAC policy, we'll document default settings and how to customize. Carlos, when you say immutable retention, do you mean append-only exported logs or do you require us to hold on your behalf?
[05:28] Carlos Reyes: for pilot export is fine: we want to pull logs into our SIEM daily; long term we may want a managed retention but pilot-export meets the immediate need
[05:36] Dr. Priya Menon: one more item — model governance and output lineage. we need a way to tie outputs to model versions and to revert to a previous variant if there's a regression
[05:46] Liam O'Connor: the runtime tags model_id and model_version in each request/response; we also support canary rollouts and automatic fallback to a smaller model when latency spikes — we'll document the rollback steps in the runbook
[05:58] Aisha Turner: regarding encryption, are customer-managed keys supported in Hosted for the pilot? you mentioned bring-your-own-key earlier but wanted to confirm the lead time
[06:08] Samira Khan: yes, BYOK via KMS is supported for Hosted pilots; we need a key ARN and a quick IAM role config, usually takes 1-2 business days to validate once we have the key and policy in place
[06:20] Jordan Park: ok let's capture the success criteria explicitly — i want to read them back: 1) security: SOC2+ISO attestation provided and shared with Elmwood; 2) SSO via Okta configured and tested; 3) RBAC mapped to AD groups with admin and developer roles; 4) audit logs exported daily and ingested by Elmwood SIEM; 5) KMS integration with customer-managed key; 6) data residency and no PHI in test data; 7) performance: p95 < 800ms for interactive, embeddings throughput target 50k/hr (example), cost estimate within agreed range. any edits?
[06:48] Carlos Reyes: change embedding target to 40k/hr for pilot to be conservative; otherwise thats fine
[06:56] Jordan Park: noted, embeddings 40k/hr. for timelines: proposed schedule: send security pack today, customer sends SSO metadata and test data by Fri 2029-06-21, run bench 2029-06-24 to 2029-06-26, review on 2029-06-28, final exec summary 2029-07-02. does that work?
[07:16] Dr. Priya Menon: yes that timeline fits our compliance window
[07:22] Aisha Turner: one operational ask — can you provide a short runbook for rollback in case a canary causes regressions? we need the exact commands and who to call
[07:32] Liam O'Connor: absolutely, we'll include a rollback runbook with exact API calls, CLI snippets, and contact list for on-call engineers.
[07:40] Samira Khan: quick note on metrics — we'll collect latency p50/p95/p99, token burn rates, cost per 1k tokens, CPU/GPU utilization, and autoscale events. we'll provide a spreadsheet with the benchmarks and costs
[07:54] Jordan Park: awesome. any competitor pressure to discuss?
[08:00] Carlos Reyes: we evaluated Anthropic and OpenAI; main reasons to consider Redwood are better controls for RBAC/peering and pricing predictability for the scale we need, also we prefer a vendor that supports BYOK and easier audit exports
[08:14] Samira Khan: makes sense, we find enterprise pilots often lean towards Private or Dedicated when security is the gating factor, but Hosted with peering + BYOK often meets pilot needs faster
[08:28] Dr. Priya Menon: ok last thing — procurement will ask for an indicative cost for the 4-week pilot, can you send a rough estimate?
[08:36] Jordan Park: yes we'll follow up with a short pilot quote and the SOW template.
[08:42] Carlos Reyes: thanks, also please include proof of any penetration tests and our ability to run an independent pen test against the staging environment
[08:50] Samira Khan: we can provide past pen test reports and allow a scheduled independent test on staging with a narrow blast radius; we'll share the process and required approvals
[09:02] Jordan Park: great. recap of next steps — i'll send security pack and SOW, samira will set up bench plan and runbook, aisha to send SSO metadata and de-id dataset, carlos to send audit fields list. we'll reconvene after bench runs. thanks everyone
[09:18] Dr. Priya Menon: thank you all
[09:20] meeting end
